prize_parts.citation: For incorporating firm heterogeneity and selection into trade theory, and thereby showing how exporter selection and reallocation across firms create new channels for the gains from trade.

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged from round 1: one part, B010, credited to Helpman and Melitz. I changed only the wording, which is now narrower. Melitz (2003) moved trade analysis from the industry to the firm. That produced a distinct mechanism: only the more productive firms export, liberalisation reallocates activity toward them, and aggregate productivity and welfare change as a result. Helpman's broader programme, including Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple on exporting versus FDI, completes the framework. The mechanism has been tested for more than twenty years on firm-level data. It also connects trade to the productivity, reallocation and micro-to-macro aggregation questions that macroeconomists care about. Round 1 moved me from B037 to B010 because B037 has no stable three-name attribution. Round 1 did not change that. The proposed triads still differ by a name (Calvo-Taylor-Woodford versus Woodford-Taylor-Gali), and Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and Gertler have claims too. I am not using the eight-member convergence on B010 as evidence of merit. It is evidence that independent assessors draw the same credit boundary, and the merit case stands on the mechanism, the evidence and the maturity. I considered a two-part configuration. I do not propose one. Adding a second part would force a split of the three-person cap or a dilution of B010, and none of the candidate pairings has a merit argument that justifies it.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is still credit. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, and Hopenhayn on firm dynamics, are precursors or parallel contributors who are not credited, and Redding is omitted from the pair. A citation can reward the integrating framework, but the Committee should say plainly that it does not claim priority over every earlier fact or model. The second reservation is that the size of the selection gains depends on parametric assumptions such as Pareto productivity draws. The qualitative mechanism does not depend on that assumption, but the welfare magnitudes do, so the citation should not state a number. The third is field balance after the 2008 trade prize. I do not think it decides the matter, but I cannot say it carries no weight. B019 has the cleaner two-name attribution and a clear mechanism, but its overlap with 2022 and its more indirect empirical identification keep it second for me. My assessment rests on my own recollection of the literature and has not been independently verified.

responses.point: Boppart keeps B019 (Kiyotaki and Moore) as his preferred part. He treats B010 as a serious alternative, and the credit disputes with Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum are one reason. He prefers B019's single mechanism with clean two-author attribution to B010's larger body of confirming evidence.
responses.response: I agree B019 has the cleaner credit line, and I ranked it third and keep it as my first alternative. But clean credit is not the only consideration. I weigh the combination of a distinct mechanism, evidence that it has been checked against data, and an attribution that survives scrutiny. On B010 the Helpman-Melitz pair does survive, because the selection mechanism and its FDI extension are clearly tied to those two. The precursor question affects wording, not who is named. For B019 the 2022 adjacency and the indirect identification of collateral amplification remain open. I would not oppose B019 if the Committee judges it distinct from the 2022 recognition. I disclose that Boppart and I co-author, and this response should not be read as deference in either direction.

responses.point: Strömberg prefers B019 with Kiyotaki and Moore, and says he is not fully settled on the order of B019 and B010. He argues that the 2022 prize rewarded banks and runs, whereas Kiyotaki-Moore concerns collateral values and asset-price feedback.
responses.response: That distinction is fair, and it is the best answer to the overlap worry about B019. The two mechanisms differ, and I do not treat the 2022 adjacency as disqualifying. The remaining difference between us is how much weight direct empirical identification should carry. For B010 the exporter premia, entry and exit, and within-industry reallocation are measurable in firm-level data. For B019 the amplification channel is mostly established through its influence on models and post-2008 crisis analysis. The question for the Committee is how much weight that gap deserves. I think it deserves enough to keep B010 first, but not so much that B019 drops out of consideration.

responses.point: Enflo prefers B032 (Autor, Hanson, Dorn). She narrowed her set from Katz to Dorn to avoid the overlap with the 2023 prize and the task-framework antecedents, and she argues that continuing debate over magnitudes shows the findings have been scrutinised, not that they are fragile.
responses.response: I agree that debate over magnitudes is not evidence of fragility, and the same applies to B010's Pareto sensitivity. In both cases the qualitative finding is the discovery and the magnitude is open. Narrowing to the trade-shock core was a sound response to the mixed-strand problem. My remaining difficulty is the chair's question of what the citation would rest on. The shift-share identification debate and the unsettled long-run aggregate welfare picture make the citation wording harder for B032 than for B010. I keep it outside my alternatives for that reason. I would reconsider only if the Committee settles which strand is the core and which claims on persistence it is willing to make.

responses.point: Hassler (chair) prefers B010 and says the citation should stay narrow, not become a lifetime-achievement framing for Helpman. He also says no clean citation exists for B037 yet, and that he would reconsider if the Committee finds a defensible boundary.
responses.response: I agree on both points, and the wording above follows the first one. Helpman's credit should rest on firm-level and FDI work with Melitz, not on a career-wide framing. On B037, the chair's round-1 question was whether a principled triad exists. After the round 1 exchange I cannot name a rule that picks Calvo, Taylor and Woodford over Woodford, Taylor and Gali, or that excludes Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and Gertler. Friberg and I drew different triads, which shows the credit is unstable. I therefore keep B037 as a second alternative, behind B019. I note that Hassler is a long-term co-author of mine, as disclosed, so my agreement with him on B010 should not be counted as independent corroboration of the credit.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee judges heterogeneous-firm trade a distinct advance beyond the 2008 recognition of new trade theory. Boppart's file treats it as a serious alternative but does not call his concern resolved.
Whether the citation can acknowledge Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum and Hopenhayn, and whether excluding Redding from the pair is accepted as a boundary.
How far the selection and reallocation gains survive productivity distributions other than Pareto. I am confident only about the qualitative mechanism.
Whether the Committee finds a principled three-name boundary for B037, and how the 2021-23 inflation episode should weigh in the assessment.
How much weight field balance after the 2008, 2022, 2023 and 2024 prizes should carry. I treat it as secondary to significance, attribution and maturity, but I do not claim it carries none.
statement.conflict_note: No connection to Helpman, Melitz or the other credited names on B010, B019 or B037 is apparent from my supplied profile. I disclose ties to committee members who are not candidates: I am a frequent co-author of John Hassler (chair) and have co-authored with Timo Boppart (co-opted member), including the 2018 Myrdal Prize article. Both are IIES colleagues, and Hassler also prefers B010. My field is heterogeneous-agent macro and growth, which is adjacent to the micro-to-macro reallocation questions in B010 and to the macro side of B037 and B019. Torsten Persson (B039) is a past Committee member. B039 is not in my preferred configuration or alternatives. These are disclosed and not adjudicated.
